header: IN THE HIGH COURT OF SINDH
DATE ORDER WITH SIGNATURE OF JUDGE
None present for the applicant; nor intimation received.
This Criminal Misc. Application has been filed for cancellation
of bail granted to the respondent No.1 by learned Additional
Sessions Judge-I, Umerkot in Criminal Bail Application No.
531/ 2026 vide order dated 10-07-2026, on the following
“I have heard learned counsel for the parties and
body: perused the material available on record. From the perusal of record it reflects that the alleged occurrence is stated to have taken place on 07.05.2026, however, the complainant did not lodge the FIR promptly. Rather, he first approached the SSP after two days of the alleged occurrence and subsequently filed an application under Section 22- A & 22-B Cr.P.C on 19.05.2026. The delay in setting the criminal law into motion has not been satisfactorily explained and prima facie calls for cautious consideration at the bail stage. It is wellsettled principle of law that unexplained delay in lodging the F.I.R creates doubt regarding the genuineness of the prosecution story and provides sufficient time for deliberation and consultation. It is also an admitted position that prior to registration of the F.I.R, the SSP Umerkot constituted an inquiry team under the supervision of DSP, who made inquiry, recorded statements of the parties and submitted a report concluding that the deceased had committed suicide due to illness. Though such inquiry report may not be treated as conclusive evidence at this stage, yet the same constitutes a relevant circumstance creating a ground for further inquiry. It is also an admitted position that before registration of the FIR, the SSP constituted a Joint Investigation Team under the supervision of DSP, which conducted a detailed inquiry after recording the statements of both parties. The inquiry report concluded that the deceased had committed suicide due to illness. Although such an inquiry report is not conclusive proof of innocence and its evidentiary value shall be determined during trial, nevertheless, at the stage of bail it constitutes a relevant circumstance creating a reasonable doubt regarding the prosecution version and cannot be ignored outright. The facts and circumstances, particularly the delayed registration of the FIR, the findings of the inquiry conducted under the supervision of a senior police officer prior to registration of the case, prima facie bring the case within the ambit of further inquiry as envisaged under Section 497(2), Cr.P.C.”

Perusal of the findings of learned trial court reflects that same are in accordance with law and no illegality or infirmity is found therein, therefore, instant Criminal Misc. Application being devoid of merits stands dismissed in limini. JUDGE “Saleem”
